stories.extended_summary: 'Bartenders take care of everyone, and sustain so many people — and we need somebody to sustain us, too,' says Keyatta Mincey, beverage director at Atlanta's Heritage Supper Club. That's the whole idea behind A Sip of Paradise Garden, a quarter-acre plot tucked into East Atlanta Village where hospitality workers come to relax, connect, and get their hands in the dirt. Mincey pitched the community garden during a global cocktail competition years ago; she didn't win that part, but when Covid hit she built it anyway. Six years later, around 30 bartenders and former hospitality workers tend over 30 plots bursting with mint, purple basil, star jasmine, prickly pear, okra, and more — some for sustenance, some for cocktail inspiration.

stories.extended_summary: The bus was rolling down a Saint Paul street at 10 mph with its doors wide open and lights flashing — a sight that stopped Ebro Ahmed cold. The 27-year-old store worker sprinted from the sidewalk and leapt onto the moving bus, where he found the driver in the middle of a medical emergency. He'd never driven a bus before, and briefly confused reverse with park, sending the bus beeping backward before he slammed it into neutral and pulled the parking brake. Behind him, scared kids were already dialing police. Ahmed credits "Grey's Anatomy" for inspiring his quick thinking.

stories.extended_summary: It all started with a 40-pound ice cream tub of kiwifruit his mom brought home. In January 2023 he researched cottage food laws, launched the next month, and now runs The Jam Man full-time with more than 60 flavors of jam, syrups, and pickles.

stories.title: Who knew subtitles could sing opera?
stories.summary: Boston's MASARY Studios has reinvented opera subtitles — projecting animated supertitles onto theater walls and scenic windows so they move with the music instead of pulling your eyes away from the stage. They debuted the tech at Boston Lyric Opera's production of Mahler's 'Song of the Earth.'
stories.extended_summary: Subtitles usually mean choosing between reading and watching. MASARY Studios just made that choice unnecessary. The Boston multimedia collective designed a "supertitles" system that projects animated text onto the theater's own architecture — a house-left brick wall, a scenic window — with fonts and motion stylized to match the music, poetry, and operatic delivery. It debuted at Boston Lyric Opera's staging of Gustav Mahler's "Song of the Earth," directed by Anne Bogart. Using a four-projector Epson setup, the team turned subtitles into another character on stage rather than a distraction from it.

stories.title: “Gathering of Ink” to celebrate Indigenous tattoo traditions, artistry in Oklahoma
stories.summary: Missy Mahan never saw Indigenous representation in the tattoo industry — so she built a three-day convention in Oklahoma City showcasing Indigenous tattoo artists, traditional tools, and artistry. 'NDN Territory Gathering of Ink' celebrates southeastern tribes and marks 20 years since Oklahoma legalized tattooing.
stories.extended_summary: Missy Mahan has been tattooing for 14 years and never saw her community represented on studio walls. So she co-founded NDN Territory Gathering of Ink, a three-day tattoo convention in Oklahoma City featuring Indigenous artists, presentations, and vendors — timed to mark 20 years since Oklahoma, the last state to legalize tattooing, lifted its ban in 2006. Mahan, who is Tohono O'odham, Yuchi, and Muscogee, is bringing her traditional cactus-spine tools and the protocols she learned from elders. "I want our artwork on the walls," she said. "I want our representation to be one of our main focuses."
